doc.title: Paul Shaffer interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, August 24, 2023

title: Dropping out of the band and depression in college
summary: Studying philosophy and sociology, bored and depressed after leaving the Fugitives, he realized something had to change.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: You were getting this amazing training for what you ended up doing in your career. Did, at some point when you were in college, did you decide I think I need to be a musician?

Yes. And it was so clear because you know I had had this outlet, I had had this band, Ricky & The Fugitives, they were called The Fugitives and I joined them they were already a band. They were a sax instrumental band and played Johnny & The Hurricanes type material, Red River Rock, and Ricky could on that stinky tenor of his play the flutter-tongue style of that period and then they started singing when The Beatles hit and then they had to hire, they hired a keyboard player, you know they expanded their sound. What — I got carried away with my own boredom. What did you ask again?
I think I was going towards some of the things you’ve said sounded like it seemed an inevitable —

Oh yes all right, well in college I was so bored I gave up the band, I no longer was a member of the Fugitives or had any outlet to perform in any way and I was trying to be a sociologist or something and I got really depressed, so depressed that I had to sleep all

the time. Nowadays imagine, you know you have Epstein-Barr Syndrome, whatever it was I just knew that if I had a class at 9 AM ‘til 10, by 10:15 I was back in bed in the dorm. I could not — so sad. And then I don’t know if we have time and my old boss would say, “Do we have to cut away?”
